title: Status page copy for planned regional failover tests vs. real incidents
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
## Context
We’re running controlled regional failover tests (“game days”) as part of the Reliability Program. We need clear, consistent status page language that:
- Distinguishes planned tests from real incidents
- Sets expectations (possible brief errors/latency) without overpromising
- Avoids creating alarm for customers who are not impacted
- Keeps updates concise and cadence-driven

This ticket covers copy only (not status page component UI). Copy must work for both Hosted API and Dedicated capacity, and must not imply data residency changes or customer-specific routing behavior.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence template: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/status-page-template-regional-event.json
- Comms playbook: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json
- PM umbrella: PM-512 (regional failover UX + customer notifications)

## Goals
1) Provide a dedicated template for PLANNED failover tests (Scheduled/Monitoring style), including a short FAQ line.
2) Tighten INCIDENT template language for real regional impairment to avoid confusion with tests.
3) Align terminology across: Status page, Console banner, and Support macros (where possible).

## Non-goals
- Defining the underlying incident policy (severity mapping, what triggers a status page post)
- Writing account-specific comms (CS handles proactive outreach for enterprise accounts)

## Copy principles (must-follow)
- Be explicit about intent: “planned test” / “controlled failover test” / “regional resilience exercise.”
- Avoid implying a degradation is expected for all customers. Use: “Some customers may experience…”
- Avoid words that sound like an ongoing outage for planned tests: do NOT use “Investigating” or “Service disruption” for planned tests.
- Keep updates short; include next-update time.
- For incidents: keep to standard incident language (“Investigating/Identified/Monitoring/Resolved”), include impact and affected components/regions.

## Proposed status page taxonomy
A) Planned test posts
- Incident type/category: “Maintenance” or “Planned Event” (depending on status page platform)
- Status progression: Scheduled → In progress → Monitoring → Completed

B) Real incident posts
- Incident type/category: “Incident”
- Status progression: Investigating → Identified → Monitoring → Resolved

---

# Deliverable: Copy templates

## A) PLANNED: Controlled Regional Failover Test (Scheduled)
**Title options (pick one):**
1) “Planned: Controlled regional failover test (us-east → eu-west)”
2) “Planned regional resilience test: controlled failover (us-east → eu-west)”
3) “Planned maintenance: regional failover exercise (Hosted API / Dedicated)”

**Scheduled (initial post)**
> We will be conducting a controlled regional failover test to validate automated failover and rollback behavior.
>
> Impact: Some customers may see brief increases in latency and/or transient errors during the test window.
>
> We will post updates here throughout the test. Next update by {time}.

**In progress**
> The controlled failover test is now in progress.
>
> We are monitoring request success rate, latency, and capacity signals while shifting traffic.
>
> Impact: Some customers may experience transient errors/timeouts or brief reconnects for streaming responses.
>
> Next update by {time}.

**Monitoring**
> The failover portion of the test has completed and traffic is stable.
>
> We are monitoring for any residual impact and will confirm completion once metrics remain within normal operating ranges.
>
> Next update by {time}.

**Completed (final)**
> The controlled failover test is complete.
>
> If you observed an issue you believe is related, please contact Support and reference this event window: {start}–{end} {timezone}.

**Optional short FAQ line (append to Scheduled + In progress)**
> FAQ: This is a planned test (not an active outage). It helps validate automated regional failover behavior.


## B) INCIDENT: Regional Impairment (Investigating)
**Title guidance:**
- Use “Service disruption” / “Degraded performance” / “Increased error rates” + region + product surface area
- Example: “Service disruption: Increased errors in us-east (Hosted API)”

**Investigating**
> We are investigating reports of increased errors and elevated latency affecting {component} in {region}.
>
> Impact: {what users observe}. We will provide an update by {time}.

**Identified**
> We have identified an issue impacting {component} in {region} and are working to mitigate.
>
> Mitigation may include shifting traffic to alternate regions where supported.
>
> Next update by {time}.

**Monitoring**
> A mitigation has been applied and we are monitoring recovery.
>
> Impact should be reduced; we will confirm resolution after metrics remain stable.

**Resolved**
> This incident is resolved and service has returned to normal operating levels.


## Component / product naming (consistent labels)
- “Hosted API” (not “Public API”)
- “Dedicated capacity” (not “Dedicated clusters”)
- “Console” only if the Console itself is impacted (avoid mentioning Console for routing tests)

## Region naming (consistent)
- Use short cloud region identifiers in parentheses if needed, but keep primary labels human-readable.
  - Example: “US East (us-east)” and “EU West (eu-west)”

---

# Open questions (resolved in this ticket)
1) Do we call this “maintenance” or “planned event”?
- Decision: Use “Planned event / Maintenance” category (platform-dependent), but copy should say “controlled failover test” to remove ambiguity.

2) Do we mention streaming reconnects?
- Decision: Yes, but only as “brief reconnects for streaming responses” (no protocol specifics).

3) Do we promise ‘no impact’?
- Decision: No. Use “Some customers may see…” to avoid overpromising and to match observed behavior in rehearsals.

---

# Acceptance criteria
- [x] Planned test template does not use incident language (Investigating/Service disruption)
- [x] Planned test template includes: intent, possible impact, update cadence, and support reference
- [x] Incident template remains standard and clearly separate from planned tests
- [x] Terminology aligned with PM-512 + Comms playbook

# Implementation notes
- Copy should be added as selectable templates in the status tooling (Devon Price / SRE tooling).
- Ensure the first line of Scheduled includes the phrase “planned” and “controlled failover test.”

2026-01-05 (Dev Patel): Support request: include a single sentence on how to reference the event when filing a ticket (time window + region). This helps triage.
2026-01-07 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated note: avoid implying all dedicated tenants are affected. ‘Some customers may…’ works; please keep Dedicated wording generic.
2026-01-10 (Allison Grant): From observability side: please mention the metrics we’re watching in general terms (success rate, latency, capacity) — that helps credibility without exposing internals.
